t: Before you stands the Queen's House, a former royal residence that is now a public art gallery. It was built between 1616 and 1635 on the grounds of the vanished Greenwich Palace. Inigo Jones designed it, and it is the first building in England in a pure classical style. Anne of Denmark, wife of James the First, commissioned it, and her successor as queen, Henrietta Maria, also commissioned Jones. It was a royal retreat for enjoying the queens' art, including a ceiling work in the Great Hall by Orazio Gentileschi. Today it forms the centrepiece of the Old Royal Naval College.
